passages.title: Welcome to the Model Railroad Club
sentences: Welcome to the Harbor Town Model Railroad Club, which meets in the basement of the Harbor Town Library.
Our layout is a model of the coast, with a working drawbridge, a ferry dock and a tunnel under Lantern Peaks.
Junior members are 11 to 15 years old, and each one works with an adult member called a crew partner.
Your crew partner will teach you how the layout works and will sign your logbook after each lesson.
Regular meetings are on Saturdays from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.
During June, however, meetings will move to Wednesdays from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM.
The library needs the basement for its summer reading camp on Saturday mornings in June.
Meetings return to Saturday mornings on the first Saturday in July.
Before you can run a train on your own, you need three signatures in your logbook.
You earn the first one for learning the track map, the second for using the control panel, and the third for a safe practice run.
Most junior members earn all three signatures in four to six meetings.
Members with three signatures may run a train at our Open House on Saturday, July 12, when families visit the layout.
Please follow these rules to keep the trains and the layout in good shape.
Wash your hands before you touch a train, because oil and dust from your fingers can clog the tiny motors.
Never reach across the track while a train is moving; walk around the table instead.
Food and drinks stay upstairs in the lobby, and backpacks go on the shelf by the door.
If you have a question, ask your crew partner or email the club at trains@example.com.
We are glad you joined, and we hope you enjoy your first season with us.

If you do not know the name of a rock, write a question mark instead, and Mr. Varga will help you find out.
The doors open at 9:30 AM so that you can set out your rocks, and trading starts at 10:00 AM.

passages.title: Dome Notes
sentences: Welcome to the November issue of Dome Notes, the newsletter for the Junior Astronomers at the Lantern Peaks Observatory.
This month brings two changes to our Thursday night meetings, so please read this issue carefully.
First, the big telescope in the dome will be closed from November 3 to November 21.
Every few years, its giant mirror must be removed and cleaned, because a thin layer of dust makes faint stars harder to see.
While the mirror is being cleaned, we will set up five small telescopes on the lookout deck instead.
The lookout deck has no roof and no walls, so please dress for wind and cold.
Second, our winter schedule begins on December 1.
As the nights grow longer, the sky gets dark much earlier, so meetings will start at 6:30 PM instead of 8:00 PM.
Meetings will still last 90 minutes, and the last bus down the hill will still leave ten minutes after each meeting ends.
The winter schedule continues until the end of February.
Finally, here is a note about how we plan our star counts.
Bright moonlight makes faint stars very hard to see, so we count stars only on nights when the Moon is thin or cannot be seen at all.
Our next star count is on Thursday, November 20, a night with no bright Moon.
Please bring a notebook, a pencil and a flashlight with a red cover, because white light makes it harder for everyone's eyes to adjust to the dark.
Dr. Lee and the observatory team look forward to a season of clear, dark skies with you.

passages.title: Welcome, Junior Volunteers
sentences: Thank you for joining the Junior Volunteer program at the Harbor Town Animal Shelter.
Junior volunteers are 11 to 15 years old, and they help us care for the cats, dogs and rabbits that are waiting for new homes.
Every junior volunteer works with an adult family member, who must stay in the same room the whole time.
Shifts are on Saturdays and Sundays, from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM or from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.
Please sign up for each shift on the paper calendar at the front desk at least two days ahead.
During your first three shifts, you will fold towels, wash food bowls and fill water dishes.
These jobs help the animals get used to you, and they help you learn how the shelter works.
After three shifts, you may also brush the cats and play with the rabbits in the small animal room.
Dog walking is only for volunteers who are 14 or older, because some of our dogs are large and pull hard on the leash.
Before you touch any animal, wash your hands at the sink by the door.
Wash them again when you move from one room to another, so that germs do not spread between the animals.
Never open a cage or a kennel by yourself; ask a staff member first.
Please wear closed shoes and clothes that can get covered in fur.
From December 1 to February 28, the afternoon shift moves to 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM, because the shelter closes earlier in winter.
Morning shifts stay the same all year.
